meta.tagline: The red city's square, gardens and never-ending theatre

pills: Jemaa el-Fnaa: the world's liveliest square
The Atlas Mountains half an hour away

overview.title: Welcome to Marrakech
overview.intro: Marrakech is less a city than a stage set: inside the red walls, snake charmers and storytellers assemble the square, the scent of copper and leather rises in the souk's narrow veins, and tiled serenity hides behind the riad doors. The snow-capped Atlas peaks glitter behind the palms — this much contrast rarely fits in one frame. Marrakech is exhausting, mesmerising and entirely unapologetic: join its tempo, but keep the addresses of the doors of calm in your pocket.

local_word.definition: The medina's dead-end alley: riads' real addresses are always inside a derb. 'At the end of the derb, the green door' is as valid as a deed in this city — getting lost is part of the address system.

rules.title: See the square twice
rules.description: Jemaa el-Fnaa is one thing by day and another entirely by night: orange-juice carts and water sellers in the afternoon, then smoke, drums and a hundred-stall open kitchen after dark. Miss either and you haven't seen the square.

rules.title: Photos have prices — know it and choose
rules.description: The square's snake charmers, monkey handlers and henna women charge per photo — often aggressively. If you don't want it, don't point the camera, avoid eye contact, keep walking; if you do, agree the price first.

rules.title: Schedule your doses of calm
rules.description: Marrakech's intensity can overdose you: write one garden, one riad courtyard or one hammam into every day. The city's secret is rhythm — chaos and serenity are both on the menu.

quick_facts.label: Airport
quick_facts.sub: ~20 min to the medina by taxi

quick_facts.label: Language
quick_facts.sub: English common on the tourist trail

quick_facts.label: Signature
quick_facts.sub: The square is UNESCO oral heritage

tip.label: The Marrakech philosophy
tip.text: Learning to say 'no' in Marrakech doubles the pleasure of saying 'yes': keep walking with a la shukran, but once a day step through an unplanned door — the city's best memories live behind those doors.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The medina on foot, the rest by little beige taxis: distances are short — keep your haggling reflexes on.

items.title: Airport to the centre
items.description: Menara is 20 minutes from town: fix the taxi price before boarding or book a riad transfer. Bus 19 is the budget friend — it calls at the square and Gueliz.

items.title: The medina on foot
items.description: The square, the souks and the palaces are within walking distance; getting lost in the derbs is part of the programme. Mopeds squeeze through even the narrow lanes — walk to the side, keep an ear behind you.

items.title: Petit taxi — the little beige ones
items.description: The vehicle for short city hops: ask for the meter, and if it stays off, agree the price first. The night tariff is higher than the day's — that's normal; don't normalise the outrageous.

items.title: The calèche — a carriage tour
items.description: A carriage ride along the ramparts is a classic pleasure: fix route and price before boarding, and choose a carriage with well-kept horses. Timed to sunset, the tour paints the red walls ember-orange.

items.title: Atlas and desert escapes
items.description: The Ourika Valley and Atlas villages are an hour away, the Agafay desert 45 minutes: plan a day with a small-group tour or private driver. Leaving the city doubles Marrakech.

callout.label: Taxi tip
callout.text: In any taxi at a medina gate, two sentences suffice: 'compteur, afak' (the meter, please) and a smile. If it stays off, get out — one that turns it on is two steps away. Ask your riad the fair short-hop fares in advance.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Marrakech you choose between two worlds: the riad serenity of the medina, or the poolside spaciousness of the new town?

local_word.definition: The traditional courtyard house: in Marrakech, hundreds have become boutique hotels. The plainer the door, the more splendid the interior tends to be — in this city wealth faces the courtyard, not the street.

items.name: Medina — around the square
items.description: Riads within walking distance of Jemaa el-Fnaa and the souks: the city's pulse at your doorstep. The square's hum may reach you at night — the price of atmosphere, with a minaret view from the terrace as reward.

items.name: Medina — Kasbah and Mellah
items.description: The district of the Saadian tombs, palace ruins and the spice square: one notch calmer than the square's bustle, dense with history. Stork nests on the ramparts are the neighbourhood's signature.

items.name: Gueliz — the New Town
items.description: French-era boulevards, cafés, galleries and shopping: the airy base for those who want distance from the medina's intensity. Walking distance to Majorelle, a short taxi to the medina.

items.name: Hivernage
items.description: The district of large pool hotels and night clubs: palm-lined avenues, spas and quiet nights. For comfort-first travellers — five minutes to the medina by taxi.

items.name: The Palmeraie and country hotels
items.description: Pool villas among the palm groves and desert camps towards Agafay: city by day, starlit silence by night. Works with a car or shuttle — a honeymoon classic.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: The red city's calendar is written by the sun: spring and autumn gold, summer a furnace, winter a sunny-cool surprise.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Orange Blossom Season
items.subtitle: Spring · Mild days, scented gardens
items.description: The gardens smell of orange blossom, snow still shines on the Atlas peaks, and the terraces are exactly right. Marrakech's best-loved window — crowds and prices to match.

callout.label: April tip
callout.text: On an April morning enter Majorelle at opening and pair it with the Yves Saint Laurent museum: the cobalt garden before the crowds is another place entirely. Buy the ticket online in advance.

items.label: Summer
items.name: The Furnace Months
items.subtitle: Summer · Noons above 40 degrees
items.description: The heat is serious: life moves to morning, night and the poolside. Prices fall and the square still fills at night — summer Marrakech is possible, provided the plan is built on shade and air-conditioning.

callout.label: July note
callout.text: In summer make no street plans between 11 and 5: souk in the morning, riad pool or hammam at noon, the square at night. Water, hat and electrolytes — the standing trio.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Golden Light
items.subtitle: Autumn · Breaking heat, clear skies
items.description: The heat breaks in September; October-November is the city's most balanced stretch: mild days, cool evenings, ideal for Atlas outings. The light turns to the tone photographers call 'Marrakech gold'.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: In October give a day to the Atlas: walnut harvest in the villages of Ourika or Imlil, clear mountain air and Berber tea. Back in the city, even the square's noise sounds sweet.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Sunny Coolness
items.subtitle: Winter · Mild days, cold nights
items.description: Sunny and jacket-warm by day, noticeably cold at night — ask your riad about heating. The classic refuge from the European winter: gardens calm, souk relaxed, and the city at its most photogenic against the snowy Atlas.

callout.label: January tip
callout.text: A terrace lunch in winter sun is Marrakech's hidden luxury: a cardigan on your back, a tagine before you, the snowy Atlas across the sky. Nobody can take that photo in summer.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Marrakech table cooks over coals and in clay: the city's signature is tanjia, the square's is smoke, and the terraces' is the sunset.

local_word.definition: Marrakech's own dish: meat, preserved lemon and spices sealed in a clay urn and cooked for hours in the hammam's ashes. Originally the Friday meal of bachelor workmen — today the city's gastronomic signature.

items.name: Tanjia — the legend cooked in ash
items.description: Meat slow-cooked in the urn falls apart in strands, the preserved-lemon scent wrapping the plate: a ritual of Marrakech, distinct from tagine. Ask for a place that makes the real thing — it's served from the urn.
items.tag: The Marrakech signature · served from the urn

items.name: The tagine variations
items.description: Lamb with prunes and almonds, chicken with lemon and olives, kefta with egg: under the conical lid every house tells a different story. Order at your riad the evening before — always a step ahead of the souk menu.
items.tag: Riad cooking · order the day before

items.name: The square's stalls — a table of smoke
items.description: The hundred-stall open kitchen assembled each evening: skewers over coals, harira, snail soup. The crowded stall is the fresh stall — memorise its number and come back tomorrow night.
items.tag: On the square at night · from the crowded stall

items.name: Moroccan salads and zaalouk
items.description: Smoky aubergine zaalouk, carrot taktouka, plates of olives: the colourful army that dresses the table before the main. Wiping with bread is the custom — the fork is optional.

items.name: Square oranges and avocado shakes
items.description: The juice carts are the square's daytime classic; the milk bars' avocado-almond shake is the locals' cooling secret. Both cost a few dirhams, both are legends.
items.tag: Daytime classic · fresh from the cart

items.name: Mint tea and Moroccan sweets
items.description: Gazelle horns (kaab el ghazal), honey-dripping chebakia and almond-paste parcels: the tea ceremony's sweet army. On a terrace, facing the sunset — state your sugar level at the start.

callout.label: The square-table rule
callout.text: At the night stalls two rules suffice: choose the stall where locals sit, and never sit without seeing the price list. The meze that arrives 'as a gift' goes on the bill — send back what you didn't ask for with a smile; that too is part of the game.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone knows Majorelle; these six are the red city's concealed courtyards.

items.name: Le Jardin Secret
items.description: A restored palace garden in the souk's middle: the water channels of Islamic garden art, a cactus collection and medina rooftops from its tower. Two steps from the chaos, a mathematical serenity.

items.name: The Maison de la Photographie terrace
items.description: The museum of old Moroccan photographs is crowned by one of the medina's finest terraces: see the collection, drink your tea on the roof, catch the Atlas on the horizon. Modest entry, generous view.

items.name: The El Badi Palace ramparts
items.description: The giant ruin of the Saadian golden age: sunken pools, orange-tree pits and storks nesting on the walls. Go early — the storks' clatter comes before the crowds' chatter.

items.name: Bahia's quiet rooms and the Saadian tombs at opening
items.description: The Bahia Palace's back courtyards and the Saadian tombs' tiled chambers are nearly empty at opening time: see the zellij and cedar ceilings without a queue. Buy the same ticket at noon and you buy the queue with it.

items.name: Rahba Kedima
items.description: The old grain square inside the main souk: spice pyramids, herbalists' shops and stalls of woven hats. The terrace cafés around it are the souk-fatigue's official remedy.

items.name: An Agafay dinner
items.description: A stony desert plateau 45 minutes from town: tented camps, camel silhouettes and sunset tables against the Atlas. 'The desert for those without time for the Sahara' — with the dinner + stars combination.

callout.label: Garden strategy
callout.text: Marrakech's gardens are toured by crowd management: Majorelle at opening, Le Jardin Secret in the midday lull, the Menara olive grove at sunset. Each garden is a shift — all three fit one day if the order holds.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Marrakech plays its games on an open stage — for those who know the rules, it's theatre, not danger.

items.name: The square's photo traps
items.description: The monkey lands on your shoulder, the snake wraps your neck, the henna touches your hand — then comes a harsh demand for payment; haggling in a crowd is hard.
items.instead: If you don't want it, keep distance, don't point the camera, avoid eye contact. If you do, agree the price clearly and have small notes ready — let both the experience and the price be your choice.

items.name: The 'souk is closed, follow me' guide
items.description: The Fes game on the Marrakech stage: the volunteer guide walks you in circles and ends the tour in a commission shop.
items.instead: 'La shukran' + keep walking. Stick to the signposted main axes; if you truly want a guide, have your riad book an officially badged one.

items.name: The 'Berber pharmacy' show
items.description: Some spice shops stage healing shows for coach groups: ordinary spices sold at multiplied prices under 'miracle' labels.
items.instead: Buy spices at the plain stalls around Rahba Kedima, watching the weighing. Real saffron is expensive — 'cheap saffron' is actually safflower.

items.name: View tax on the terrace + bill surprises
items.description: Some square-facing terraces sell an average menu at view prices and enjoy adding lines to the bill.
items.instead: Use the terrace for sunset tea, and eat one lane in or at your riad. Checking the bill line by line isn't rude here — it's custom.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: In Marrakech every 'gift', every 'free' and every 'just to look' is an opening line: smile, say la shukran, walk. Then once a day, through a door of your own choosing, enter the haggle — the game's pleasure works for those who know its rules.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: A full red-city day, from garden to square

steps.title: Majorelle at opening
steps.description: Be first into the cobalt garden; then a short dive into the YSL museum. You're out before the crowds are in.

steps.title: The Koutoubia and into the medina
steps.description: Walk from the minaret's shadow to the ramparts and enter the medina by the Kasbah gate: the Saadian tombs' tiled chambers are still calm.

steps.title: A tanjia lunch
steps.description: Tip the ash-cooked tanjia from its urn onto the plate: Marrakech's signature meal. Mint tea on top, half an hour in the shade.

steps.title: The souk and Le Jardin Secret
steps.description: Get lost in the spice pyramids and the leather and copper veins; when tired, breathe in the secret garden's water-channelled courtyard.

steps.title: Sunset tea on a terrace
steps.description: Climb to the Maison de la Photographie's roof: sip tea as the medina rooftops turn red — below, the square is already assembling.

steps.title: A Jemaa el-Fnaa night
steps.description: Smoke, drums, story circles and the hundred-stall kitchen: dinner at a crowded stall, then lose yourself in the square's theatre.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: City, palaces and mountain — three acts

steps.title: Classic Marrakech
steps.description: The one-day flow above: Majorelle, Kasbah, tanjia, souk, the square at night.

steps.title: Palaces and the hammam
steps.description: The Bahia Palace + El Badi's stork-topped walls in the morning; a meze crawl around Rahba Kedima at noon; a traditional hammam + rest in the afternoon; modern Moroccan cooking in Gueliz at night.

steps.title: Atlas or Agafay
steps.description: Pick your day: Berber villages and walnut valleys at Imlil, or a desert sunset table at Agafay; one last farewell loop of the square on return — orange juice in hand, drums behind you.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Five words of Darija work on the Marrakech stage as both shield and key.

items.meaning: Hello — the greeting that opens every exchange
Thank you — double effect with a smile
'No, thank you' — the square's and the souk's shield; said while walking
'How much?' — the line that opens the haggling curtain
'Okay, deal' — the haggle's happy ending; sealed with a handshake

checklist.completion_message: Wakha! You've done the red city properly!
